question: Which Federal Reserve Governors gave speeches on stablecoins or tokenization in 2025 and 2026, and what was each one's main point?
answer:
Taking "2025 and 2026" to mean speeches dated January 1, 2025 through October 1, 2026, and "Governors" to mean Board of Governors speakers (excluding the Chair): five Governors—Michael S. Barr, Christopher J. Waller, Stephen I. Miran, Lisa D. Cook, and Michelle W. Bowman—gave 11 speeches squarely on stablecoins or tokenization in that window, plus two borderline speeches that mention the topics but are not primarily about them.

## Speeches squarely on stablecoins or tokenization

| Speaker | Date | Title / Venue | Main point |
|---|---|---|---|
| Christopher J. Waller | 2025-02-12 | "Reflections on a Maturing Stablecoin Market," A Very Stable Conference, San Francisco | Stablecoins are an important innovation with potential to improve retail and cross-border payments; the market is maturing, and to be economically viable they must show both a clear use case and a clear commercial case, with challenges to full potential examined from a public-sector perspective [D2]. |
| Michelle W. Bowman | 2025-08-19 | "Embracing Innovation," Wyoming Blockchain Symposium 2025, Teton Village, WY | Banks of all sizes, including community banks, can benefit from efficiency gains from asset tokenization, which can enable direct, faster, lower-cost payments; with the GENIUS Act now law, stablecoins are positioned to become a fixture in the financial system with implications for traditional banking and payment rails [D1]. |
| Christopher J. Waller | 2025-08-20 | "Technological Advancements in Payments," Wyoming Blockchain Symposium 2025, Teton Village, WY | The Fed should continue embracing technological advancements to modernize its services and support private-sector innovation, including research on tokenization, smart contracts, and AI in payments, and deepen engagement with industry innovators as the traditional financial sector and digital-asset ecosystem converge [D3]. |
| Christopher J. Waller | 2025-09-29 | "The Next Frontier of Payments Innovation," Sibos, Frankfurt | Emerging technologies—stablecoins, tokenization, and AI—define the next frontier in global payments innovation. |
| Michael S. Barr | 2025-10-16 | "Exploring the Possibilities and Risks of New Payment Technologies," D.C. Fintech Week | New payment technologies, including stablecoins, offer real efficiency and inclusion benefits but carry risks (run vulnerability, illicit finance, market disruption) that require a careful, risk-based regulatory approach. |
| Christopher J. Waller | 2025-10-21 | "Embracing New Technologies and Players in Payments," Fed Payments Innovation Conference | The Fed should embrace new technologies and new market participants in payments. |
| Stephen I. Miran | 2025-11-07 | "A Global Stablecoin Glut: Implications for Monetary Policy," BCVC Summit | If stablecoins grow as the industry expects, they become a "multitrillion dollar elephant in the room" for central banks, with major monetary-policy implications for reserve demand and dollar internationalization. |
| Lisa D. Cook | 2026-05-08 | "Perspectives on Tokenization and Implications for the Financial System," BCEAO Conference on Digital Assets, Dakar, Senegal | Tokenization could offer compelling benefits—faster cross-border payments and better access to capital markets, especially in West Africa and other emerging economies—and reduce frictions in settlement, recordkeeping, and automation, but its opportunities and financial-stability challenges warrant careful central-bank consideration [D4]. |
| Michael S. Barr | 2026-03-31 | "Brief Remarks on Stablecoins," Federalist Society | Discusses implementation of the GENIUS Act and key open questions for stablecoin regulation. |
| Christopher J. Waller | 2026-09-29 | "Payments in the Age of AI Agents," Sibos, Miami | AI agents will reshape payments (agentic commerce, cross-border efficiency), with stablecoins one rail among many that agents may use. |

## Borderline speeches (mention stablecoins/tokenization but not primarily about them)

- **Christopher J. Waller**, "Welcoming Remarks on the International Role of the U.S. Dollar," 2026-06-22 — notes that distributed ledger technologies and tokenized assets such as stablecoins are creating new channels for global dollar intermediation.
- **Lisa D. Cook**, "An Assessment of the Economy and Financial Stability," 2025-01-06, Michigan Law — includes a financial-stability section on stablecoins: they lack a comprehensive federal regulatory framework, are structurally vulnerable to runs, and their role in intermediation chains (leverage, collateral) warrants monitoring.

## Notes on coverage and confidence

- The main points for Barr (2025-10-16, 2026-03-31), Waller (2025-09-29, 2025-10-21, 2026-09-29), and Miran (2025-11-07) are inferred from titles, venues, and the passages retrieved, not from full-text reading of each speech; the Barr, Waller 2025-02-12, Waller 2025-08-20, Cook 2026-05-08, and Bowman 2025-08-19 points are drawn directly from the evidence excerpts above.
- The search relied on title and content searches across the collection's 186 speeches; a speech with an unrelated title that nonetheless discusses stablecoins or tokenization could have been missed.
- Checked and excluded as not on stablecoins/tokenization: Kevin Warsh's "In Our Time" (Jackson Hole, 2026-08-28), Waller's "Innovation at the Speed of AI" (2025-10-15), "Modernizing Federal Reserve Operations" (2026-04-21), "Update on Federal Reserve Bank Operations" (2026-05-08), and "Operationalizing AI at the Federal Reserve" (2026-02-24), Barr's "Efficient and Effective Central Banking" (2026-05-14) and "Promoting Responsible Innovation through the Novel Activities Program" (2025-02-27, crypto-asset banking only in passing), and Bowman's 2026 speeches (AI, stress testing, eSLR, cyber).
